fields.evaluation.heading: How to Evaluate a Titanium Dioxide Grade
fields.evaluation.step.1.title: Define the application
fields.evaluation.step.1.body: Record the resin or material system, end use, processing conditions and performance targets that the grade must be evaluated against.
fields.evaluation.step.2.title: Confirm whether process matters
fields.evaluation.step.2.body: Identify whether chloride or sulfate production-process classification is a required sourcing parameter. Process classification does not determine application suitability.
fields.evaluation.step.3.title: Review applicable technical data
fields.evaluation.step.3.body: Review information issued for the grade you are evaluating. Do not infer missing values from another grade, an older source or an unrelated TDS.
fields.evaluation.step.4.title: Identify destination and document needs
fields.evaluation.step.4.body: Confirm the destination market and the technical, quality, compliance or origin documents required for the applicable request.
fields.evaluation.step.5.title: Validate in the buyer's system
fields.evaluation.step.5.body: Confirm final suitability through the buyer's own formulation, processing conditions, performance requirements and qualification process.
fields.support.heading: Continue Your Procurement Review

fields.support.card.2.title: Identify Required Documents
fields.support.card.2.body: Review technical, quality, compliance and origin-document pathways for the applicable request.
fields.support.card.3.title: Review Destination Context
fields.support.card.3.body: Review destination-market procurement context without assuming local availability, registration or regulatory acceptance.
fields.faq.heading: Buyer Questions
fields.faq.item.1.question: How do I choose a titanium dioxide pigment grade?
fields.faq.item.1.answer: Start with the intended application, then use production-process classification if it is a required sourcing parameter. Review the relevant grade page and confirm the available product information against the formulation, processing conditions, destination and documentation requirements. A listed result is a starting point for evaluation, not a suitability guarantee.
fields.faq.item.2.question: Which grades are listed in this product center?
fields.faq.item.3.question: What is the difference between application and process selection?
fields.faq.item.3.answer: Application selection groups grades by listed use-case relationships, while process selection groups grades by their production-process classification. A process classification does not determine application suitability on its own.
fields.faq.item.4.question: What if no grade is shown for my application?
fields.faq.item.4.answer: A missing result means that the selector has no listed grade for that application. It should not automatically be interpreted as a technical rejection of every grade. Buyers can contact the team when a requirement is not represented in the selector.
fields.faq.item.5.question: Does a listed grade guarantee suitability?
fields.faq.item.5.answer: No. A listed grade is a starting point for technical evaluation. Final suitability should be confirmed against the buyer's formulation, processing conditions, performance requirements, destination requirements and applicable documentation.
fields.final-rfq.heading: Request a Quote for Your Requirements
